Thanks Ellen — appreciate the clear list. I've skimmed the redlines and put together an annotated pass that calls out three operational tradeoffs: uptime measurement window, maintenance blackout carveouts, and the credit aggregation formula. See attached SLA_Annotated_By_Redwood.docx (high level notes inline).

Quick summary of our proposed positions so procurement/legal can react:

- Measurement window: We measure availability at the customer account level with a 30-day rolling window. For distributed apps, we'll define availability per-region and provide a consolidated view for billing.
- Maintenance: We propose two lanes — (1) Scheduled maintenance (30-day rolling scheduled notifications; agreed weekly windows per region) which does not trigger credits when notified with X hours; (2) Emergency maintenance (security/hotfix) — we propose this is excluded from credits if declared and reasoned, but limited to events that cannot be deferred.
- Credits cap: Redwood proposes a 12% cap in any 12-month period for availability credits, with a per-event floor to avoid micro-credits.

Action items: can we set a 30-minute sync early next week with StellarNet Legal/Procurement and Redwood Product + Legal? Lauren, Aditya — looping you for legal/ops input.

Attachments: SLA_Annotated_By_Redwood.docx (notes + suggested edit snippets)

Dylan

Ellen / team — Aditya from Redwood legal and product here. Thanks for sending the redlines. I went into the specific Exhibit A items and the primary open negotiation points I think we can close without executive signoff are:

1) Response times and P1 definition:
   - Proposed Redwood response windows: P1 (system-down impacting production) — respond within 1 hour, P2 (severe degradation) — respond within 4 hours, P3 — next business day.
   - We want the SLA to define "impacting production" in terms of customer-defined production endpoints and error-rate thresholds — I included suggested wording in the attached docx.

2) Maintenance window scheduling:
   - We can agree to a weekly maintenance window per region (2 hrs weekly) that customers can opt into for non-peak operations. For customers that require blackout periods, we can offer an exception process: a rolling 90-day blackout calendar where Redwood will not schedule non-emergency maintenance. That exception requires a 60-day advance notice and is subject to capacity constraints.

3) Credits calculation and cap:
   - We propose a tiered credit model (1–3 hours -> 3% credit, 3–8 hours -> 8% credit, >8 hours -> 12%) with an annual cap of 12% of monthly recurring charges. We've kept thresholds intentionally conservative; if StellarNet needs a higher cap, that pushes to executive review.

Notes and asks for StellarNet: please confirm whether your production traffic is primarily concentrated in us-west/us-east so we can align maintenance windows accordingly. Also, Marcus — if you can point us to any non-negotiable language StellarNet Legal requires on force majeure or emergency maintenance carveouts, we'll incorporate exact phrasing.

I've included tracked snippets in SLA_Annotated_By_Redwood.docx. Happy to join the sync.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Counsel (Contracts) — Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick confirmation from our side after internal review:

- StellarNet operations are primarily us-west with a DR cluster in eu-west. The blackout calendar request is reasonable; procurement will review the 60-day notice requirement but it's within our standard playbook.
- On credits cap: Procurement prefers a 15% annual cap but Legal can accept Redwood's tiered approach if we have clearer aggregation language for repeated short outages. Please add a sentence that clarifies how multiple incidents in a 30-day rolling window are aggregated (we prefer additive up to the cap rather than per-incident reset).
- Emergency maintenance carveout: Legal will provide exact force-majeure language, but for now we accept the principle that properly declared emergency maintenance may be excluded from credits; we want a post-event report within 72 hours.

Let's do the sync Wednesday 2026-06-09 10:00 AM PT — Marcus, Ellen, Procurement team; Dylan, Aditya, Lauren and Redwood ops. Marcus will circulate a short agenda and a copy of the procurement checklist.
